construct: real <table> markup: thead/tbody row GROUPS, whose UA display is `table-header-group` / `table-row-group` - a formatting context with no box of its own
why: `display: table` on a div is already pinned REFUSED (display-out-of-vocab). This case is the OTHER half of the same archetype and the one every real data table actually ships: the row-group wrappers the UA stylesheet creates, which are neither `table` nor any display value in the carried vocabulary. A data table cannot be proven without knowing what happens to thead/tbody, and the answer must be a NAME, because a row group that is silently flattened takes the header/body distinction with it.

canvas.note: AutoLayout has no table formatting context and no row-group concept

mustHave: if the case is refused, the refusal names the table/row-group construct in LEDGER.md
nothing is emitted that claims to be a table but has lost the header/body distinction
a grader reading the receipt can tell WHICH construct was refused, not merely that something was

predictedWall.why: AMENDED before any run. In the sealing commit I predicted the row groups would be flattened SILENTLY and proposed a new code for it. A vocabulary survey then found the mechanism I had missed: extract/computed/anatomy.ts has `lowerTableDisplay`, which handles 'table-header-group' and 'table-row-group' BY NAME and emits the receipt prefixes `table-lowering:`, `table-geometry-excluded:` and `control-fallback: no control for <thead> - span control used`. All four strings are visible verbatim in examples/mui/contracts/table.extension.json:4379-4418. So the honest prediction is now that this case PASSES - the groups are lowered to a flex stack and NAMED - and I have withdrawn the proposed code rather than leave a claim of 'no name exists' standing against a name that does. What remains genuinely un-named is narrower and I am not testing it here: `fuse.table-column-arity-disagreement` drops width AND height for EVERY cell of the whole table on any colspan, whose counter-example in the register reads 'Any colspan in the corpus disables column widths table-wide.'
